constraints: No new PR, merge, deploy, or release
Prefer user value over speculative breadth

candidates.name: YAML semantic change review before apply
candidates.user_value: High: users can see what a whole-document YAML apply will change, not only how page 1 renders.
evidence: src/app/yaml-source-dialog.tsx renders only the first-page visual preview
Apply sends the complete parsed DesignDocument
The existing stale-revision guard protects concurrency but not unintended valid edits
DSA-PROD-001 identified whole-document replacement as residual risk
candidates.risk: Low-to-medium; summary accuracy and large-document presentation require explicit limits

candidates.name: Accessibility preflight accuracy
candidates.user_value: High for design quality and accessibility.
evidence: src/shared/design-checks.ts labels contrast as estimated and excludes compositing, opacity, animation, and font-specific metrics
candidates.complexity: Medium-to-high because exact compositing and rendered text measurement cross renderer boundaries
candidates.risk: Could falsely imply certification; needs a separate research checkpoint

candidates.name: Dependency security remediation
candidates.user_value: Important maintenance/security value but less directly visible to the core design workflow.
evidence: npm audit reports eight high-severity findings through Cloudflare Puppeteer, Wrangler/Miniflare/Sharp, and PptxGenJS/image-size chains
candidates.complexity: High and multi-owner; suggested downgrades can be breaking or misleading
candidates.risk: Broad regression surface across rendering, Workers, and export

candidates.name: Real-time collaboration presence
evidence: Current editor uses polling and optimistic merge/revision semantics without presence
candidates.complexity: Very high; persistence, transport, presence, and conflict UX redesign
candidates.risk: Speculative and not bounded enough for the next checkpoint

selection: DSA-PROD-006 — YAML Semantic Change Review Specification
rationale: It closes the clearest post-launch safety gap in the newly merged capability while reusing current parsing, schema, preview, and revision semantics and avoiding persistence/API redesign.
